set1.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 72-year-old man with exertional angina is admitted with two weeks of worsening breathlessness, orthopnea, leg swelling and bibasilar crackles. Blood pressure is 118/70 mmHg and heart rate is 84 beats per minute. Which antianginal is contraindicated in this condition?
opts: Atenolol
Correct. Acute decompensated heart failure is a contraindication to a beta blocker, because its negative inotropic effect can push a congested patient into worse failure.
Isosorbide dinitrate
Nitrates lower preload and are not barred by heart failure. Their contraindications are aortic stenosis, obstructive cardiomyopathy and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors.
Amlodipine
Among calcium channel blockers it is the accepted choice when ventricular function is reduced, unlike verapamil and diltiazem, which are avoided in heart failure.
Sublingual nitroglycerin
It relieves an acute attack by venodilation and heart failure does not forbid it. Hypotension and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors are what limit its use.

set1.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia
set1.q: A 63-year-old man with stable exertional angina had a myocardial infarction three years ago. Heart rate is 70 beats per minute and blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg. He has no asthma and no conduction disease. In the traditional comorbidity-based approach, which class is best avoided?
opts: Beta blockers
A beta blocker is first line after an infarction and is the class preferred here, so it is not the one to avoid.
Long-acting nitrates
These are adjuncts that can be added when symptoms persist; they are not the class avoided after an infarction.
Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors
These are continued indefinitely after an infarction to slow disease progression, so they are not avoided here.
Calcium channel blockers

Correct. The traditional comorbidity table says to avoid calcium channel blockers after an infarction and to prefer a beta blocker. Current practice is less absolute and allows a non-dihydropyridine when a beta blocker cannot be used and ventricular function is normal.

set1.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 52-year-old man has sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the back and ST-segment elevation. Blood pressure differs between the two arms, and imaging shows an aortic dissection. Which drug is contraindicated?
opts: Metoprolol
A beta blocker lowers heart rate and shear stress on the aortic wall, and dissection does not forbid it.
Labetalol
It blocks alpha and beta receptors to lower pressure and heart rate and is used in dissection.
Tenecteplase
Correct. Aortic dissection is a contraindication to fibrinolysis, because clot lysis can lead to catastrophic bleeding.
Morphine
It is an analgesic and aortic dissection does not forbid it.

set1.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 65-year-old man with stable angina has type 2 diabetes mellitus and a reduced ejection fraction of 35 percent. He takes aspirin and metoprolol. Which added drug may slow progression of his coronary disease?
opts: An angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor
Correct. It is used in coronary disease with diabetes or left ventricular systolic dysfunction and may prevent disease progression, though it does not relieve angina.
A long-acting nitrate
It relieves angina but does not slow progression of coronary disease, and it is an adjunct rather than a vasculoprotective drug.
A dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker
It treats symptoms and does not alter disease progression. With reduced ejection fraction, amlodipine is the calcium channel blocker that is accepted.
A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker
With a reduced ejection fraction it is contraindicated, because it depresses contractility and can worsen heart failure.

set1.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 70-year-old man has 40 minutes of chest pressure at rest. The electrocardiogram shows ST-segment depression without ST elevation, and the cardiac biomarker is elevated. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: ST-elevation myocardial infarction
This diagnosis requires ST-segment elevation, which is absent here.
Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Correct. No ST elevation with a raised biochemical marker separates a non-ST-elevation infarction from unstable angina.
Unstable angina pectoris
It has the same electrocardiogram pattern but no rise in the biochemical marker, which is elevated here.
Chronic stable angina pectoris
Stable angina is exertional and brief and does not raise cardiac biomarkers.

set1.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 55-year-old woman started a new antianginal two weeks ago. She now has a throbbing headache, facial flushing and swelling of both ankles. She has no dyspnea or orthopnea, and her jugular venous pressure is normal. Which drug class best explains these findings?
opts: A dihydropyridine
Correct. Headache, flushing and peripheral edema are the typical effects of the dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, which dilate arterioles strongly.
A beta blocker
Beta blockers cause fatigue, bradycardia, nightmares and hyperglycemia. Peripheral edema with flushing points elsewhere.
A non-dihydropyridine
Verapamil and diltiazem act mainly on the heart and cause constipation and bradycardia, with much less vasodilator headache, flushing and edema.
A long-acting nitrate
Nitrates cause headache and flushing but not the ankle edema, which is the distinguishing feature of a dihydropyridine.

set1.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 56-year-old man with an ST-elevation myocardial infarction was treated with streptokinase for a previous infarction years ago. He has no bleeding history. Which fibrinolytic should be avoided now?
opts: Alteplase
A recombinant tissue plasminogen activator, a different agent from streptokinase, so prior streptokinase exposure is not the listed contraindication.
Streptokinase
Correct. Prior streptokinase exposure or a previous allergic reaction to it is a listed contraindication to using it again.
Reteplase
A recombinant product and a different agent from streptokinase, so prior streptokinase exposure is not the listed contraindication to it.
Tenecteplase
A recombinant product and a different agent from streptokinase, so prior streptokinase exposure is not the listed contraindication to it.

set1.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 54-year-old man with an acute coronary syndrome still has chest pain after aspirin. Blood pressure is 130/82 mmHg and he takes no phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor. Which drug relieves his pain but does not improve survival?
opts: Aspirin
It reduces mortality, reinfarction and stroke, so it is a survival therapy and not just an analgesic.
Metoprolol
It lowers heart rate and oxygen demand and is given for outcome benefit, not as a drug whose only job is pain relief.
Nitroglycerin
Correct. Nitrates give chest pain relief with no mortality benefit, starting sublingually and moving to an intravenous infusion in hospital.
Clopidogrel
An antiplatelet that reduces clotting events. It does not relieve pain.

set1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia
set1.q: A 70-year-old man with stable angina opened his bottle of sublingual nitroglycerin tablets eight months ago. He keeps it in the original container in a bedroom drawer and has used it twice. In the traditional counseling, what should he be told about the tablets?
opts: Keep using them until the bottle is empty
Nitroglycerin is unstable, and waiting for the bottle to empty risks a degraded tablet in an emergency; the traditional advice is to replace opened tablets every 3 to 6 months.
Move them to a weekly pill organizer
The tablets belong in the original packaging in a cool, dry place, because light and moisture degrade them; a pill organizer is the wrong storage.
Replace them with a fresh supply

Correct. The traditional counseling is to replace opened tablets about every 3 to 6 months so that a potent tablet is ready in an emergency. Current labeling ties expiry to the printed date when the tablets stay in the tightly closed original glass bottle.
Refrigerate them to extend their life
Refrigeration is not the instruction; the tablets are kept cool and dry in the original packaging and replaced about every 3 to 6 months.

set1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for myocardial ischemia drug therapy
set1.q: A 57-year-old woman with an acute coronary syndrome received intravenous metoprolol in the emergency department. Heart rate is now 64 beats per minute, blood pressure is 126/74 mmHg, and she has no heart block or wheezing. In the traditional sequence, what is the next step in her beta blocker therapy?
opts: Stop the beta blocker now
The intravenous dose is the start of therapy, not the whole of it; the traditional sequence continues with an oral beta blocker.
Switch to an oral beta blocker
Correct. The traditional sequence is an intravenous beta blocker followed by an oral one once she is stable. Current guidelines favor starting oral therapy within the first day.
Add a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker
A beta blocker with a non-dihydropyridine risks excess bradycardia and block, and calcium channel blockers are not the next step; the sequence continues with an oral beta blocker.
Repeat intravenous doses for several days
The traditional sequence is intravenous followed by oral, not prolonged intravenous dosing; she moves to an oral beta blocker once stable.

set1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 66-year-old woman keeps her sublingual nitroglycerin tablets in a weekly pill organizer on the bathroom counter. Which storage instruction is correct?
opts: Weekly organizer, away from sunlight
Removing the tablets from the original container is the error, and the humid bathroom makes it worse. The original packaging is the standard.
Original container, cool and dry place
Correct. The tablets are stored in their original packaging in a cool, dry place so that they stay potent. The bathroom's moisture is the problem here.
Refrigerator door, in a sealed bag
Refrigeration is not the instruction. The storage point is original packaging kept cool and dry, and cold, damp conditions are not required.
Car glove box, within easy reach
Heat in a parked car degrades the tablets. The original container in a cool, dry place is the correct instruction.

set1.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 55-year-old man presents two hours after the onset of crushing chest pain. The electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. He has no bleeding history, no prior stroke and no recent surgery. Which drug restores coronary flow by dissolving the clot?
opts: Enoxaparin
It limits propagation of the thrombus, but it does not lyse an established clot.
Clopidogrel
An antiplatelet that prevents further aggregation and does not dissolve the clot.
Alteplase
Correct. A fibrinolytic activates plasminogen bound to fibrin, dissolving the clot in an early ST-elevation myocardial infarction with no contraindication.
Nitroglycerin
It relieves pain through vasodilation and does not restore flow by lysing the thrombus.

set1.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 68-year-old man with stable angina takes atenolol. His exertional chest pain persists. Pulse is 64 beats per minute, and the electrocardiogram shows normal conduction. Which added drug carries the greatest danger of symptomatic bradycardia and heart block?
opts: Amlodipine
Dihydropyridines act on vessels and leave atrioventricular conduction unchanged, so they are the calcium channel blocker added to a beta blocker.
Felodipine
Another dihydropyridine, so it is vasoselective. It does not slow the atrioventricular node, and this is why it pairs safely with a beta blocker.
Isosorbide mononitrate
A nitrate dilates vessels and may raise heart rate reflexively. It does not slow conduction, so it is a safe adjunct to a beta blocker.
Verapamil
Correct. A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker also slows the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes, so adding it to a beta blocker risks bradycardia and block.

set1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for myocardial ischemia drug therapy.
set1.q: A 57-year-old man is starting a beta blocker for stable angina. Which set of findings should be followed?
opts: Potassium, creatinine, blood pressure
That panel fits drugs acting on the kidney and potassium. A beta blocker's effects are on heart rate, glucose and lipids.
Heart rate, blood sugar, lipids
Correct. Beta blockers slow the heart and can raise blood glucose and worsen lipid profiles, so all three are monitored.
Platelet count, hemoglobin, bleeding
That is the safety check for antiplatelet and fibrinolytic therapy, not for a beta blocker's heart rate, glucose and lipid effects.
Liver enzymes, thyroid tests, weight
None of these is the routine follow-up for a beta blocker, whose adverse effects are bradycardia, hyperglycemia and dyslipidemia.

set1.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 58-year-old man has an ST-elevation myocardial infarction two hours after onset. Blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg and heart rate is 82 beats per minute. He vomited blood and passed black stools this week, and a gastroscopy found a bleeding ulcer. Which drug class should be avoided?
opts: A beta blocker
It lowers heart rate and oxygen demand and does not affect bleeding risk.
A nitrate
It dilates vessels and does not impair hemostasis, so bleeding does not forbid it.
An opioid analgesic
It does not interfere with clotting, and bleeding is not a contraindication to it.
A fibrinolytic
Correct. Active bleeding and serious recent gastrointestinal hemorrhage are fibrinolytic contraindications, because these drugs break down clots and raise bleeding risk.

set1.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 57-year-old man with ST-elevation myocardial infarction still rates his pain 9 out of 10 after repeated sublingual nitroglycerin. Blood pressure is 124/76 mmHg. Which drug is used for chest pain unresponsive to nitrates?
opts: Metoprolol
It lowers heart rate and oxygen demand and is given for outcome benefit; it is not the analgesic for pain that persists despite nitrates.
Morphine
Correct. It is the opioid analgesic used for pain unresponsive to nitrates in ST-elevation infarction, though its use is controversial.
Clopidogrel
An antiplatelet, it reduces clotting events and does not treat pain.
Enoxaparin
An anticoagulant that limits clot propagation, it has no analgesic effect.

set1.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 58-year-old man with stable angina uses sublingual nitroglycerin as needed. He asks to start tadalafil for erectile dysfunction. What is the main danger of combining them?
opts: Profound hypotension
Correct. Nitrates raise cyclic guanosine monophosphate and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors block its breakdown, so vasodilation is exaggerated, risking hypotension, infarction or stroke.
Bradycardia with heart block
Conduction block is the danger of a beta blocker combined with verapamil or diltiazem. Here the danger is excessive vasodilation.
Loss of nitrate effect
Tolerance comes from continuous nitrate exposure. This combination does the opposite, intensifying the nitrate's vasodilator effect.
Bronchospasm
Airway narrowing is a non-selective beta blocker concern. Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors with nitrates threaten blood pressure.

set1.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 24-year-old college athlete has exertional chest pain and near-syncope. A systolic murmur grows louder with the Valsalva maneuver, and echocardiography shows asymmetric septal hypertrophy with outflow obstruction. Which drug class would be harmful?
opts: A beta blocker
Obstructive cardiomyopathy is not among the listed contraindications for a beta blocker; the nitrates are the class to avoid.
A non-dihydropyridine
Obstructive cardiomyopathy is not among the listed contraindications for these agents. The nitrates are the class contraindicated here.
A nitrate
Correct. Obstructive cardiomyopathy is a listed nitrate contraindication, and aortic stenosis is the other structural one.
An antiplatelet drug
It does not change ventricular filling or outflow, so the obstruction does not forbid it; the vasodilating nitrates are the concern.

set1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 63-year-old man is started on verapamil for exertional angina because a beta blocker was not tolerated. Which adverse effect should he be counseled about?
opts: Vivid nightmares
Nightmares are a beta blocker effect. Verapamil acts on calcium channels and is better known for constipation and dizziness.
Raised blood sugar
Hyperglycemia is a listed beta blocker effect and is not the expected problem with a calcium channel blocker.
Bronchospasm
Airway narrowing is a concern with non-selective beta blockers. Calcium channel blockers do not provoke it, which is why they are used in asthma.
Constipation
Correct. Dizziness and constipation are the listed counseling points for calcium channel blockers, so he should expect and plan for constipation.

set1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 53-year-old man's exertional angina resolves within minutes of a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet. Which effect most directly lowers the oxygen demand of his heart?
opts: Beta-1 blockade slows the heart
Beta blockers reduce demand that way. Nitrates do not slow the heart and may raise the rate reflexively.
Slowed atrioventricular node conduction
This is the action of verapamil and diltiazem, not of nitrates, which work on vascular smooth muscle.
Blocked calcium entry into the heart
That is the calcium channel blocker mechanism. Nitrates act through nitric oxide and cyclic guanosine monophosphate.
Venodilation lowers ventricular volume
Correct. Nitrates generate nitric oxide, which relaxes vascular smooth muscle; venodilation lowers filling and wall tension, which reduces oxygen demand.

set1.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 66-year-old man with stable angina and peripheral vascular disease is about to start a beta blocker. Which adverse effect is he most at risk of?
opts: Worsened pain when walking
Correct. Worsened claudication is a listed beta blocker adverse reaction, and peripheral vascular disease is a listed precaution for the class.
Constipation with hard stools
Constipation is an effect of calcium channel blockers, especially verapamil, not of beta blockers.
Swelling of both ankles
Peripheral edema is typical of the dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, not of beta blockers.
Throbbing headache on standing
Headache with flushing and postural hypotension is typical of nitrates, not of beta blockers.

set1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 68-year-old man wears a nitroglycerin patch around the clock. After several weeks his exertional angina returns despite the same patch. Which change best restores its effect?
opts: A second patch at night
More continuous nitrate exposure deepens tolerance, which is the cause of the lost effect. The remedy is a break, not extra drug.
Daily aspirin added
Aspirin helps prevent acute coronary syndrome but does nothing to reverse nitrate tolerance.
A daily nitrate-free interval
Correct. Continuous exposure causes tachyphylaxis, so a patch-free interval, such as twelve hours on and twelve hours off, restores the response.
Ointment around the clock
Changing the formulation but keeping the exposure continuous preserves the tolerance. A scheduled nitrate-free interval is what works.

set1.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 60-year-old man with stable angina still has exertional attacks three times a week on metoprolol alone. Heart rate is 66 beats per minute, blood pressure is 140/84 mmHg, and conduction and ventricular function are normal. Which added drug best relieves his symptoms?
opts: Verapamil
Adding a non-dihydropyridine to a beta blocker raises the risk of bradycardia and heart block, so a dihydropyridine is the combination partner.
Felodipine
Correct. When a beta blocker alone fails, a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker is added, because it lowers wall tension without slowing conduction.
Enalapril
An angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor does not relieve angina symptoms, although it may slow disease progression in selected patients.
Clopidogrel
It is an antiplatelet that helps prevent acute coronary syndrome. It has no effect on oxygen demand or on exertional symptoms.

set1.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 61-year-old man with stable angina has a history of hives and wheezing after taking aspirin. Which drug should replace aspirin to prevent acute coronary syndrome?
opts: Enoxaparin
It is an injectable anticoagulant used in acute coronary syndrome, not a long-term oral replacement for aspirin.
Isosorbide mononitrate
A nitrate treats symptoms and does not prevent acute coronary syndrome, so it cannot stand in for an antiplatelet.
Metoprolol
It lowers demand and helps after an infarction, but it is not an antiplatelet and does not replace aspirin.
Clopidogrel
Correct. It is as effective as aspirin for secondary prevention and is recommended when a patient is allergic to aspirin.

set1.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set1.q: A 56-year-old man with exertional angina stopped his beta blocker because of vivid nightmares and fatigue. Heart rate is 74 beats per minute and blood pressure is 134/82 mmHg. He has no asthma, conduction disease or heart failure. Which drug should replace it?
opts: Diltiazem
Correct. A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker is the initial therapy when a beta blocker is not tolerated, and he has no contraindication to it.
Carvedilol
It is still a beta blocker, so it belongs to the class he could not tolerate; the substitute comes from a different class.
Isosorbide dinitrate
A long-acting nitrate is adjunctive and not recommended as monotherapy; it leads only when beta blockers and calcium channel blockers cannot be used.
Clopidogrel
It is an antiplatelet that helps prevent acute coronary syndrome and does not lower oxygen demand, so it cannot replace an antianginal.

set2.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 64-year-old man with stable angina takes verapamil. His clinician adds simvastatin for hyperlipidemia, and three weeks later he reports diffuse muscle pain and weakness. Which interaction explains his symptoms?
opts: Lowered simvastatin levels
Inhibiting the clearing enzyme raises, not lowers, simvastatin exposure, and low levels would not cause muscle toxicity.
Raised simvastatin levels
Correct. Verapamil inhibits CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4), the enzyme that clears simvastatin, so statin levels rise and the risk of muscle toxicity increases.
Additive atrioventricular block
That is the danger of verapamil combined with a beta blocker. A statin does not slow conduction and does not cause muscle pain through this route.
Faster verapamil clearance
Simvastatin does not induce the enzymes that clear verapamil; the interaction runs the other way, with verapamil slowing the clearance of simvastatin.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 58-year-old man has had squeezing chest pressure on climbing stairs for three months, relieved within minutes by rest. He had a myocardial infarction two years ago. Heart rate is 76 beats per minute and blood pressure is 132/80 mmHg. He has no asthma and no conduction disease. Which drug class is first-line daily therapy to prevent further attacks?
opts: A long-acting nitrate
Nitrates are adjuncts, not monotherapy. They come first only when beta blockers and calcium channel blockers are contraindicated or not tolerated, which is not this patient.
A dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker
These are added when a beta blocker alone has failed to control symptoms. They are not chosen ahead of a beta blocker in a patient with no contraindication.
An angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor
It can slow progression of coronary disease but does not relieve angina, so it cannot be the drug chosen to prevent the attacks themselves.
A beta blocker

Correct. Beta blockers are first-line for chronic stable angina when nothing forbids them, and they are favored after a myocardial infarction. They lower heart rate and contractility, which cuts oxygen demand.

set2.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 57-year-old man with hypertension and stable angina has a blood pressure of 154/94 mmHg and a heart rate of 82 beats per minute. His clinician plans a calcium channel blocker. Which calcium channel blocker should be avoided?
opts: Short-acting nifedipine
Correct. Its abrupt vasodilation causes hypotension and reflex tachycardia, which can worsen ischemia, so short-acting agents are avoided in angina.
Long-acting nifedipine
The extended-release form gives a smooth, sustained effect without the abrupt drop in pressure, so it is acceptable when combined with a beta blocker.
Amlodipine
A long-acting dihydropyridine with a steady effect and little change in heart rate, so it is an appropriate choice rather than one to avoid.
Felodipine
A long-acting dihydropyridine, acceptable for angina. It is the short-acting nifedipine preparation, not this class, that is the concern.

set2.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 49-year-old man takes metoprolol daily for exertional angina. He has felt well for weeks and plans to stop the tablets. Which counseling point is most important?
opts: Keep the tablets in the original bottle
That storage advice belongs to sublingual nitroglycerin, which loses potency; it is not the main safety point for a beta blocker.
Never stop it suddenly
Correct. Rapid discontinuation of a beta blocker is to be avoided, so it is stopped only on the advice of the prescriber rather than on the patient's own.
Eat extra fiber to prevent constipation
Constipation is the counseling point for verapamil and diltiazem. Beta blockers cause fatigue and dizziness instead.
Place one tablet under the tongue
That is how a sublingual nitrate is used during an attack. Metoprolol is a daily oral medicine and is not taken under the tongue.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 62-year-old man has exertional angina and severe asthma needing daily inhaled bronchodilators. Heart rate is 78 beats per minute, blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, ventricular function is normal, and there is no conduction disease. Which is the most appropriate initial antianginal?
opts: Diltiazem
Correct. A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker is the initial therapy when a beta blocker is contraindicated or not tolerated, and it does not provoke bronchospasm.
Propranolol
A non-selective beta blocker can trigger bronchospasm, so it is avoided in severe asthma. The calcium channel blocker is the alternative first-line choice.
Isosorbide mononitrate
Long-acting nitrates are adjunctive and not recommended as monotherapy. They lead only when beta blockers and calcium channel blockers cannot be used.
Enalapril
An angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor does not relieve angina. It is added for diabetes or ventricular dysfunction to slow disease progression.

set2.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 60-year-old woman receives alteplase for an ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Two hours later she has a sudden severe headache, vomiting, confusion and right-sided weakness. Which adverse effect is most likely?
opts: Ventricular arrhythmia
It is a known fibrinolytic effect, but it presents with palpitations or collapse rather than a headache and a focal deficit.
Intracranial hemorrhage
Correct. Bleeding is the main risk of fibrinolytics, and this sudden headache with a focal deficit points to intracranial hemorrhage.
Anaphylactic reaction
It causes hypotension, wheeze and swelling within minutes and does not cause headache with focal weakness.
Allergic skin rash
A rash with fever is an allergic effect and does not cause a neurologic deficit.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 58-year-old man has substernal pressure whenever he climbs two flights of stairs, relieved by a few minutes of rest. This pattern has been unchanged in frequency and severity for two years, with no rest pain. The resting electrocardiogram is normal and cardiac biomarkers are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Unstable angina
Unstable angina means new-onset, worsening or rest symptoms, and this pain has been predictable and unchanged for two years.
Variant angina
Variant angina occurs at rest, often at night, in younger patients, rather than being brought on by exertion.
Chronic stable angina
Correct. Exertional pressure that is relieved by rest, has been stable for two years and comes with normal biomarkers is chronic stable angina, graded by the activity that provokes it.
Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
An infarction causes prolonged pain with raised biomarkers, and the biomarkers here are normal.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia
set2.q: A 59-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus has exertional angina. She has no history of myocardial infarction, heart failure or hypertension, and no asthma. Heart rate is 76 beats per minute and blood pressure is 124/76 mmHg. In the traditional comorbidity-based approach, which class is first line?
opts: A non-cardioselective beta blocker
This is the type the traditional table avoids in diabetes, because beta blockers can raise blood sugar and mask hypoglycemia.
A dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker
A dihydropyridine is first line with bradycardia or atrioventricular block, which she does not have; in diabetes the traditional first line is a non-dihydropyridine.
A short-acting nitrate
Short-acting nitroglycerin is for relief of an attack and is not a daily preventive; the traditional first line for prevention in diabetes is a non-dihydropyridine.
A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker

Correct. With diabetes and no other reason for a beta blocker, the traditional table gives a non-dihydropyridine as first line; a long-acting nitrate or a cardioselective beta blocker is the alternative. Current practice is more flexible and still accepts a cardioselective beta blocker first.

set2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for myocardial ischemia drug therapy.
set2.q: A 63-year-old woman has exertional angina three times a week despite maximally tolerated metoprolol plus amlodipine. Blood pressure is 122/74 mmHg and heart rate is 62 beats per minute. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Adding verapamil
A non-dihydropyridine added to a beta blocker risks bradycardia and heart block, and more drugs should not be stacked before further workup.
Coronary angiography
Correct. Persistent angina on two antianginals prompts further workup, such as angiography, before more drugs are stacked on top.
Switching to short-acting nifedipine
Short-acting agents are avoided in angina because abrupt vasodilation and reflex tachycardia can worsen ischemia.
Stopping both for a nitrate alone
Long-acting nitrates are not recommended as monotherapy, and this would give up two agents that are already part of the regimen.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 61-year-old man with stable angina develops chest pressure while carrying groceries. Heart rate is 80 beats per minute and blood pressure is 136/84 mmHg. He takes metoprolol, amlodipine and isosorbide mononitrate every day. Which drug should he use to stop this attack?
opts: Metoprolol
A daily beta blocker prevents attacks by lowering demand, and it has too slow an effect to be the drug taken to stop one.
Amlodipine
A daily calcium channel blocker is for prevention and is not used to abort an attack that has already begun.
Isosorbide mononitrate
A long-acting nitrate is prophylactic and slow in onset; only the short-acting sublingual form is used for acute relief.
Nitroglycerin spray
Correct. Short-acting nitroglycerin under the tongue is the drug for quick relief of an attack; the daily drugs are for prevention.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 58-year-old man with a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction is taken for percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent. Which drug class is used before the procedure and to prevent clots on the stent?
opts: A glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor
It is not routinely recommended before the procedure; the P2Y12 receptor antagonists are the agents used before it and after stent placement.
A fibrinolytic
It is not recommended in non-ST-elevation syndromes because the bleeding risk exceeds the benefit.
A P2Y12 receptor antagonist
Correct. These antiplatelet drugs are used before percutaneous coronary intervention and as clot prophylaxis after stent placement.
A nitrate
It relieves chest pain through vasodilation and does not prevent clots forming on a stent; the P2Y12 receptor antagonists do.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 36-year-old woman with no cardiac risk factors wakes at 4 a.m. with severe chest pressure at rest. The electrocardiogram shows transient ST-segment elevation that resolves after sublingual nitroglycerin, and cardiac biomarkers are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Variant (Prinzmetal) angina
Correct. Vasospastic angina occurs in younger patients with few risk factors, often at night or in the early morning, with transient ST-segment elevation.
ST-elevation myocardial infarction
An infarction causes persistent elevation with a biomarker rise, while here the elevation resolved and the biomarkers are normal.
Chronic stable angina
Stable angina is brought on by exertion and relieved by rest, rather than occurring at rest in the early morning hours.
Unstable angina
Unstable angina is not defined by transient ST elevation that resolves with nitroglycerin in a young patient with attacks at night; that picture is vasospasm.

set2.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 63-year-old man with an acute coronary syndrome has a heart rate of 54 beats per minute, blood pressure of 118/72 mmHg and second-degree heart block on the electrocardiogram. Which drug should be withheld?
opts: Aspirin
Bradycardia and heart block do not restrict it. Allergy, recent gastrointestinal bleeding and recent intracranial hemorrhage do.
Metoprolol
Correct. A beta blocker needs caution with bradycardia and heart block, and this patient has a slow heart rate and second-degree block.
Sublingual nitroglycerin
Its listed restrictions are hypotension and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, and this patient has a normal blood pressure and takes no such drug.
Enoxaparin
An anticoagulant whose concern is bleeding, not conduction, so heart block does not call for withholding it.

set2.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 63-year-old man has three hours of chest pressure. The electrocardiogram shows ST-segment depression, and the cardiac biomarker is elevated. He has no bleeding history. Which therapy is not recommended for him?
opts: Aspirin
It is used in both ST-elevation and non-ST-elevation syndromes and reduces mortality and reinfarction.
Metoprolol
Beta blockers are common therapy for both syndromes when no contraindication exists.
Reteplase
Correct. Fibrinolytics are not recommended in non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome, because the bleeding risk outweighs the benefit.
Enoxaparin
It is a recommended anticoagulant in non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome, so it is not the therapy to withhold.

set2.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 59-year-old man with exertional angina is given nitroglycerin tablets for attacks. How should he be told to take one?
opts: Place it under the tongue
Correct. Short-acting nitrates are applied or sprayed under the tongue, which gives rapid onset for an acute attack.
Swallow it whole with water
Swallowing delays absorption, which defeats the purpose of a rapid-relief tablet. Short-acting nitrates are used sublingually.
Chew it, then swallow
Chew and swallow is the instruction for aspirin at the first signs of chest pain. Nitroglycerin is absorbed under the tongue.
Crush it into his food
Mixing it into food slows and reduces absorption. The tablet is meant to dissolve under the tongue for fast relief.

set2.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 74-year-old man has exertional chest pressure and two episodes of syncope. A crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur radiates to the carotids, and echocardiography confirms severe aortic stenosis. Which drug is contraindicated for his chest pain?
opts: Aspirin
Aspirin is given to prevent acute coronary syndrome in ischemic heart disease and aortic stenosis does not forbid it.
Clopidogrel
It is an antiplatelet alternative to aspirin. A fixed valve obstruction is not a contraindication to it.
Metoprolol

It does not share the nitrate contraindication. The listed contraindications for a beta blocker are a heart rate under 60, systolic pressure under 100, atrioventricular block and acute decompensated heart failure.
Nitroglycerin
Correct. Aortic valve stenosis is a listed nitrate contraindication, because the vasodilation they cause is poorly tolerated with a fixed outflow obstruction.

set2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for myocardial ischemia drug therapy.
set2.q: A 64-year-old man with known angina develops chest pressure at rest. He sits down and places one nitroglycerin tablet under his tongue. Five minutes later the pain is unchanged. What should he do next?
opts: Wait an hour to see if rest helps
Waiting delays care for what may be an infarction. The instruction is to call emergency services when the first dose has not relieved the pain.
Swallow a long-acting nitrate tablet
Long-acting nitrates are prophylactic adjuncts with a slow onset and are not rescue therapy for an attack that has not responded.
Take his beta blocker early
A beta blocker lowers demand over time and does not rescue an unrelieved attack. Emergency services are needed first.
Call emergency services
Correct. Chest pain unrelieved five minutes after the first nitroglycerin dose is treated as a possible acute coronary syndrome, so emergency help is called.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 69-year-old man has exertional angina, a heart rate of 46 beats per minute and second-degree atrioventricular block on the electrocardiogram. Which antianginal is most appropriate?
opts: Atenolol
A beta blocker slows the heart and conduction, so bradycardia and atrioventricular block contraindicate it.
Verapamil
A non-dihydropyridine slows atrioventricular conduction and must be avoided in this patient.
Diltiazem
It also depresses the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes, so it is avoided with heart block and a heart rate below 60.
Amlodipine
Correct. With bradycardia or atrioventricular block, a dihydropyridine is first-line, because it acts on vessels and does not slow conduction.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 58-year-old man has had crushing chest pressure with sweating for 30 minutes, and the ambulance crew records ST-segment elevation. He has no allergy and no bleeding history. Which drug reduces mortality and reinfarction and is given first?
opts: Sublingual nitroglycerin
It relieves chest pain but has no mortality benefit, so it is given for symptoms, not as the life-saving first step.
Oral metoprolol
Beta blockers are given in acute coronary syndrome when nothing forbids them, but aspirin is the drug given first at the first signs of chest pain.
Chewed aspirin
Correct. Aspirin is given at the first signs of chest pain, chewed and swallowed, and it reduces mortality and reinfarction.
Intravenous morphine
It treats pain that persists despite nitrates and is controversial in acute coronary syndrome, so it is not the first drug.

set2.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 61-year-old man develops fever, chills and a skin rash shortly after a fibrinolytic infusion for a myocardial infarction. There is no bleeding and blood pressure is stable. Which agent was most likely given?
opts: Streptokinase
Correct. Fever, chills and rash are allergic reactions mainly seen with streptokinase, the bacterial protein.
Alteplase
A recombinant tissue plasminogen activator. Fever, chills and rash are linked mainly with streptokinase rather than with this agent.
Tenecteplase
A recombinant tissue plasminogen activator. Fever, chills and rash are linked mainly with streptokinase rather than with this agent.
Heparin
It is given alongside fibrinolysis to limit clotting, and its chief risk is bleeding, so it does not explain fever, chills and rash.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 44-year-old woman with well-controlled asthma, treated with a daily inhaled corticosteroid and an albuterol rescue inhaler, has exertional angina. She has no bradycardia or conduction disease. Which beta blocker is most appropriate?
opts: Metoprolol
Correct. It is beta-1 selective, so it has less effect on the airway beta-2 receptors that matter in asthma. Non-selective agents are the ones to avoid in reactive airway disease.
Propranolol
It is non-selective and blocks bronchial beta-2 receptors, which can trigger bronchospasm. Non-selective beta blockers are avoided in asthma.
Nadolol
It is non-selective, so it carries the same bronchospasm risk as propranolol. A beta-1 selective agent is chosen when a beta blocker is needed in asthma.
Labetalol
It is a third-generation agent that blocks beta-1 and beta-2 receptors along with alpha receptors, so it is not cardioselective and is not the safe choice in asthma.

set2.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 66-year-old man has chest pressure at rest and an electrocardiogram suggesting an acute coronary syndrome. He had an intracranial hemorrhage last week. Blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg and heart rate is 80 beats per minute. Which of the following is contraindicated?
opts: Nitroglycerin
Its listed restrictions are hypotension and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, and a recent intracranial hemorrhage is not one of them.
Metoprolol
Its listed cautions are bradycardia, hypotension, heart block and severe reactive airway disease, and this patient has none of them.
Aspirin
Correct. Recent intracranial hemorrhage is a listed contraindication to aspirin, along with allergy and recent gastrointestinal bleeding.
Morphine
Its listed adverse effects are hypotension and allergy, and it does not impair clotting, so the hemorrhage is not the concern.

set2.io: Identify indications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia
set2.q: A 61-year-old man with ST-elevation myocardial infarction has received chewed aspirin and sublingual nitroglycerin. Heart rate is 88 beats per minute, blood pressure is 134/82 mmHg, the lungs are clear, and there is no heart block or asthma. In the traditional approach, which added class is given to lower early mortality?
opts: A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker
Calcium channel blockers are not credited with a mortality benefit after an infarction, and the traditional table lists them as a class to avoid after one.
An opioid analgesic
Morphine treats pain that nitrates do not relieve and is not credited with improving outcomes, so it is not the class that lowers mortality.
A beta blocker

Correct. A beta blocker is traditionally added, intravenous first and then oral, and is credited with lower early and late mortality when heart rate and pressure allow. Current guidelines favor oral therapy in the first day.
A long-acting nitrate
Nitrates relieve chest pain with no mortality benefit, so adding another does not lower early mortality.

set2.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used to treat myocardial ischemia.
set2.q: A 34-year-old woman is diagnosed with variant angina after recurrent nighttime rest pain with transient ST-segment elevation. Which class should be avoided?
opts: Calcium channel blockers
They relieve vasospasm and reduce symptoms, so they are a treatment of choice in variant angina.
Beta blockers
Correct. In variant angina beta blockers may worsen symptoms, so calcium channel blockers and nitrates are used instead.
Long-acting nitrates
They dilate the coronary arteries and relieve vasospasm, so they are an appropriate therapy in this condition.
Sublingual nitroglycerin
It relieves the spasm during an attack, and is the usual rescue drug, not one to avoid.
